Phase 1 RCA / re-verification before repair:

Step 0(a): duplicate sweep found closed `94a3-1323-3497-4f59` (same title/plan, implementation already on current `origin/main`) and open duplicate `3691-d673-2e4b-413a`; this ticket remains the operator-assigned work item.
Step 0(b): no version was quoted in the report; using `created_at=1788160411083998001` gives reported-against floor `5697f2e11179`. The only suspect-path change from that floor to current `origin/main` was `44ec1c2e6737` (async gate start), not a material-diagnostic change.
Step 0(c): worktree `debug-0561` is at `8db373933654c7c21fa214565426f562ca55cd80`, equal to `origin/main`.

Confirmed mechanism: bug 330c (`9ba1e90e3ccc`, ticket `330c-1c85-5bd4-48b5`) correctly normalized AC checkbox state out of the material fingerprint, making tick-only edits attestation-safe, but the attestation diagnostic surfaces still needed component-level data/reasons so a stale-material refusal could say what actually changed instead of the old fixed list. Current `origin/main` contains the broad 94a3 implementation, but the strengthened AC still found the exact misleading fixed-list literal surviving in runtime source prose (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py`), so the final repair removes that literal from `src/` and pins the grep to zero offenders.

Defect legitimacy: defect / diagnostic regression. The ticket itself gives operator-approved intended behavior: every attestation error must say what changed, and tick-only AC checkbox edits must be safe. No gate outcome change is in scope.

Attribution: `caused_by=330c-1c85-5bd4-48b5` as an unmet diagnostic obligation created when checkbox normalization changed the behavior without updating stale-material explanations enough to disambiguate checkbox-only vs material edits. I recorded the caused_by edge separately as well; the close will also pass `--caused-by`.
